transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I can’t get this thought out of my head. I’ve been an electrician for years, and if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m not safe for anyone—people I work with, people at home.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions or rituals to try and get rid of these thoughts?
I don’t think so. Not like… rituals, no. I mean, I might check things at work more than once, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Do you feel like you have to check things at work more than once because something bad might happen if you don't?
I’m… not really sure. I do check, but I don’t know if it’s because I think something bad will happen or if it’s just… habit from the job. I don’t want to make mistakes.
Do you think the thought about not being able to keep your brother safe is something you want to think about, or does it feel like it's invading your mind?

It’s not something I want to think about. It just… comes in, and then I’m stuck with it. Like if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, after all these years doing this work, then maybe I’m a danger to anyone around me. At work, at home… I don’t know.
Do these thoughts about not keeping your brother safe feel like they are forcing their way into your mind without you wanting them to?

Yeah. I mean… I’m not trying to think about it. I’ll be wiring a panel or hear my nephew shut the garage door, and it just hits me. Like I’m back there smelling smoke, seeing my brother, and everything else kind of drops out.
Do you feel like these thoughts about not keeping your brother safe are a part of you, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?

It feels like it’s mine. Not like a voice or something outside.

It’s just… this belief I can’t get away from. That if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, after all my years doing electrical work, then maybe I’m not safe for people to be around. At work, or at home.
Do you feel relieved or less anxious when you check things at work more than once?
I don’t know. Maybe for a minute, but it doesn’t really feel like relief. It’s more like… I have to do it, and then I can move on. Sort of.
Do you feel like checking things more than once is something you do to try and reduce your anxiety?
I’m not sure. I guess it might be part of it, but it doesn’t feel that clear to me. It’s more like I just… don’t feel okay moving on unless I check.
Do you think the thoughts about not being able to keep your brother safe are in line with how you really feel about yourself?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I came in because I can’t shake it — that if all my years doing electrical work couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to people who work with me… or live under my roof.
Do these thoughts about not keeping your brother safe cause you significant distress?

Yeah. It does. I mean… that’s pretty much why I came in. I can’t shake this idea that if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, after all my years doing electrical work, then maybe I’m dangerous to people around me. People I work with… people at home.
Do you try to ignore or suppress these thoughts about not keeping your brother safe when they come into your mind?

Yeah… I try not to get into it. I’ll avoid the garage unless I really have to, and I stopped helping with the electrical stuff at church. If people start talking about car projects or the fire, I usually just shut it down.
Do you think these thoughts about being a danger to others are something you'd call 'your own thoughts' or do they feel foreign to you?
They feel like mine. I mean… I don’t want them, but they don’t feel foreign. It’s my own head telling me that if I couldn’t keep my brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to people around me.
Do you feel like checking things more than once is something that helps reduce your anxiety about not being able to keep others safe?
I’m not sure. I mean, I do check things sometimes, but I don’t know if it really helps. Maybe for a minute, then it’s just… still there.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are in conflict with how you truly see yourself?

Yeah… it does. I don’t think I’m someone who wants to hurt anybody. But I can’t shake the thought that if all my years doing electrical work didn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to people who work with me… or even live under my roof.
Do you think these thoughts about being a danger to others are something you want to have or something that is unwelcome to you?

It’s unwelcome. I don’t want to think that way… but it keeps coming back, that if I couldn’t keep my brother safe after all my years doing electrical work, then maybe I’m dangerous to people around me.
Do you feel like you have to perform specific actions to try and get rid of the anxiety caused by these thoughts?
I don’t know… not really specific actions, I guess. Sometimes I do things to feel a little less on edge, but I’m not sure it actually gets rid of it.
Do you feel like the idea of being a danger to others is something that aligns with your own values and beliefs about yourself?

No… not really. I don’t see myself as someone who wants to hurt people. It’s more like… I can’t get past the idea that if all my years as an electrician didn’t keep my brother safe, then maybe I’m not safe for people around me. People I work with, or people at home.
Do you feel like you are trying to neutralize or balance out the bad thoughts about not keeping your brother safe with your actions, like checking things more than once?
I’m not sure. I do check things sometimes, yeah… but I don’t know if I’m trying to “balance it out” exactly. It’s more just… I feel uneasy, and I look again. Then I still feel uneasy.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a danger to others are something that you would consider a part of your own personal beliefs and values?

I don’t think it’s what I believe about myself, exactly. I don’t want to be dangerous to anyone. It’s just… I can’t shake the thought that if I couldn’t keep my own brother safe, after all my years doing electrical work, then maybe I’m a danger to people who work with me or live under my roof.
Do you think these thoughts about not keeping your brother safe started right after the incident or did they develop over time?

I think it started pretty soon after. Maybe it got louder over time, but… that thought’s been there since then. Like if all my years as an electrician couldn’t keep my own brother safe, then maybe I’m a danger to people around me. People I work with, or anyone under my roof.
